title: Three of the frontend's add-a-document error messages are worded differently from the messages DR1 states, including telling the trader to "Select a file to upload" where DR1 says "Upload a document".

finding.frontend: The four messages the add form can produce are held in one block (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:63-81). One matches DR1 word for word — "Enter a document reference". Three do not: the missing date reads "Enter the date of issue", the missing file reads "Select a file to upload", and an unparseable date reads "Enter a real date of issue". No captured frontend state shows any of them; they are read from the copy file, and the validators that fire them are in the same feature (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/form/errors.js:21-41).
finding.prototype: DR1's blank-form state, captured at dr1-upload-documents-error, shows the same three fields failing with "Enter a document reference", "Enter a date of issue" and "Upload a document", each linked from the summary to its field; the invalid-date message is "Enter a real date" (app/routes.js:9101-9155). The wording is identical whether the trader presses "Save and add another" or "Save and continue" — dr1-upload-documents-continue-error shows the same three strings.
finding.difference: Align the three strings in the English and Welsh copy files: "Enter a date of issue", "Upload a document", "Enter a real date". Nothing else moves — the same validators fire in the same order against the same fields. One of the three is worth a designer's eye rather than a blind copy: the frontend's "Enter a real date of issue" names the field and DR1's "Enter a real date" does not, which is the only case here where the frontend's wording is the more specific of the two.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting the frontend's add-a-document form blank and reading "Upload a document" and "Enter a date of issue" in the error summary.
